1. An ancient statue from the Huasteca region of Mexico represents a subject not seen before in artifacts from the area: a woman in an assertive stance wearing items used in a ceremonial ballgame. Archaeologist Maria Eugenia Maldonado notes that this image of a powerful athlete ____ the idea that women in pre-Columbian societies held only passive roles.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
A) reveals
B) predicts
C) forgets
D) challenges

2. Artists affiliated with the Judson Dance Theater in the 1960s were dancers (including Arlene Rothlein) and creators from other fields (such as sculptor Richard Morris) interested in redefining the concept of dance. Rejecting formal techniques, the group ____ everyday movements: many pieces were built around ordinary actions, like sitting.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
A) contrived
B) amended
C) repudiated
D) foregrounded

3. Quantitative analysis of vast historical data sets and other tools of abstraction allow historians to examine broad phenomena, but such methods ____ the particularity of individual actors. By focusing on singular individuals and incidents in exhaustive detail, Laurel Thatcher Ulrich's A Midwife's Tale and other microhistories aim to show how broader phenomena were experienced at a human level.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
A) preempt
B) misconstrue
C) efface
D) accentuate

4. Whatever the general attitude toward Clarence Brown's 1949 film Intruder in the Dust and William Greaves's 1968 film Symbiopsychotaxiplasm, Take One when they were initially released, both films now tend to be regarded quite ____. In 2018, for example, critics for the New York Times praised the former as "essential" and the latter as "a vital artifact of its time."
